question: Any natural mass of mineral matter that makes up the earth's crust is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rock.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A rock is any naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of one or more minerals or mineraloids that makes up the Earth's crust. (चट्टान — पृथ्वी की भूपर्पटी का प्राकृतिक खनिज पदार्थ)

 

• Rocks are broadly classified into three types based on their mode of formation: Igneous rocks (formed by cooling and solidification of magma/lava), Sedimentary rocks (formed by deposition and compaction of sediments), and Metamorphic rocks (formed by transformation of existing rocks under heat and pressure).

 

• The study of rocks is called Petrology, and the continuous process by which one rock type transforms into another is called the Rock Cycle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A mineral is a naturally occurring inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition and crystalline structure, whereas a rock is typically an aggregate of one or more minerals.

 

• Examples of common rocks include granite (igneous), sandstone (sedimentary) and marble (metamorphic).

 

NOTE

 

• Garbage (Option 1): Refers to waste material and has no geological meaning; it is not a mineral aggregate forming the crust.

 

• Stone (Option 3): A general/informal term often used loosely for pieces of rock, but it is not the precise geological term for the mass of mineral matter making up the crust.

 

• Fossil (Option 4): The preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms, not the mineral matter that constitutes the crust itself.

question: Rajashree Shirke was given which of the following prestigious dance awards of 2013 for her excellence in Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Academy Award.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajashree Shirke, a noted exponent of the Kathak dance form, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2013 in recognition of her excellence in Kathak. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार — कथक नृत्य)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is the highest Indian recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama, established in 1952.

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, traditionally associated with North India and storytelling through rhythmic footwork, spins (chakkars) and expressive gestures (abhinaya).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi also confers the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship), its highest honour, in addition to the annual Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar).

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri (Option 2): A civilian award conferred by the Government of India for distinguished contribution in various fields, not the specific award conferred on her in 2013 for Kathak.

 

• Kalidas Samman (Option 3): A prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh government for contributions to classical music, dance and theatre, but not the award she received in 2013.

 

• National Film Award (Option 4): Given for excellence in Indian cinema, unrelated to a Kathak dance honour.

question: Who was the captain of the Indian hockey men's team at Olympic 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manpreet Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manpreet Singh captained the Indian men's hockey team at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic). (मनप्रीत सिंह — भारतीय हॉकी टीम के कप्तान)

 

• Under his captaincy, India won the bronze medal, defeating Germany 5-4, ending a 41-year wait for an Olympic hockey medal (India's last hockey medal before this was at the 1980 Moscow Olympics).

 

• Manpreet Singh plays as a midfielder and hails from Mithapur, Jalandhar, Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian women's hockey team, captained by Rani Rampal, finished at a historic 4th place at the Tokyo Olympics 2020.

 

• P.R. Sreejesh was the goalkeeper of the men's team and played a crucial role in the bronze-medal win.

 

NOTE

 

• Amit Rohidas (Option 2): A defender in the Indian hockey team at Tokyo 2020, but not the captain.

 

• Sreejesh Ravindran (Option 3): (P.R. Sreejesh) was the team's goalkeeper, not the captain.

 

• Krishan B Pathak (Option 4): Served as the second/reserve goalkeeper for the team, not the captain.

question: An exponent of Hindustani classical music, Gangubai Hangal was an eminent singer to have hailed from the ____________ gharana of the Hindustani Khyal family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gangubai Hangal was an eminent Hindustani classical vocalist belonging to the Kirana Gharana of Khyal singing. (किराना घराना — गंगूबाई हंगल)

 

• She was a disciple of Sawai Gandharva, himself a prime disciple of Ustad Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of the Kirana Gharana.

 

• Known for her deep, powerful voice reminiscent of a male vocalist, she was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1971) and Padma Vibhushan (2002).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kirana Gharana is known for its emphasis on raga elaboration (alap) and microtonal precision; other famous exponents include Sawai Gandharva and, later, Bhimsen Joshi.

 

• Other major gharanas of Hindustani Khyal singing include Gwalior (the oldest), Patiala, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, and Rampur-Sahaswan.

 

NOTE

 

• Patiala (Option 1): Founded by Ustad Ali Bux Khan and Fateh Ali Khan; famous exponents include Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

 

• Agra (Option 3): Known for its nom-tom style of alap; famous exponents include Faiyaz Khan.

 

• Gwalior (Option 4): The oldest of the Khyal gharanas, associated with the lineage of Tansen; exponents include Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

question: If we deduct depreciation from GNP the measure of aggregate income that we obtain is called ______.
option_1: Gross Domestic Product at market prices
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net National Product.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net National Product (NNP) is obtained by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from Gross National Product (GNP). (शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद घटाया मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Formula: NNP = GNP − Depreciation.

 

• GNP itself equals GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA), so NNP accounts for both the wear-and-tear of capital and income earned by residents abroad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Net National Product at factor cost is also called National Income (NI).

 

• Personal Income is the total income actually received by individuals/households from all sources before payment of direct taxes.

 

NOTE

 

• Gross Domestic Product at market prices (Option 1): The value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory during a year, valued at market prices — it does not involve deducting depreciation from GNP.

 

• Gross Domestic Product (Option 2): Measures output within domestic boundaries only, without adjusting for depreciation or foreign income.

 

• Personal income (Option 4): Derived from National Income after further adjustments (like subtracting corporate taxes and undistributed profits and adding transfer payments), not simply GNP minus depreciation.

question: The chemical formula of borax is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Borax, also known as sodium tetraborate decahydrate or sodium borate, has the chemical formula Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O. (बोरेक्स — सोडियम टेट्राबोरेट डेकाहाइड्रेट)

 

• It is a white crystalline mineral salt of boron, mined from evaporite deposits formed in seasonal lakes.

 

• Borax is widely used as a flux in metallurgy/soldering, in the manufacture of glass, ceramics and enamel, as a water softener, an antiseptic, and in laboratories for the borax bead test to identify metal ions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Borax is also called suhaga in Hindi and has traditional use in Indian cuisine (as a preservative, now restricted) and in jewellery-making as a flux for soldering gold and silver.

 

• On heating, borax loses its water of crystallisation to form anhydrous borax (Na₂B₄O₇), which further decomposes to sodium metaborate and boric anhydride (B₂O₃).

 

NOTE

 

• Na₂B₅O₇·10H₂O (Option 1): Incorrect formula — borax contains four boron atoms per formula unit, not five.

 

• Na₂B₄O₇·5H₂O (Option 3): Incorrect — borax crystallises with ten molecules of water of crystallisation, not five.

 

• Na₂B₄O₇·12H₂O (Option 4): Incorrect — the correct number of water molecules of crystallisation is ten, not twelve.

question: OYO partnered with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to launch a rural tourism initiative. What this initiative is called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crown of Incredible India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2022, the Jammu & Kashmir administration partnered with hospitality company OYO to launch a rural home-stay/tourism initiative called 'Crown of Incredible India'. (क्राउन ऑफ इंक्रेडिबल इंडिया — जम्मू-कश्मीर ग्रामीण पर्यटन पहल)

 

• The initiative aims to promote rural tourism and encourage entrepreneurship/self-employment, especially among youth, by developing home-stays in rural and lesser-explored areas of Jammu and Kashmir.

 

• It was launched as part of the broader push for home-stay tourism in J&K, aligning with the Union Territory's tourism policy to diversify beyond traditional destinations like Srinagar and Gulmarg.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• OYO (On Your Own) is an Indian multinational hospitality chain founded by Ritesh Agarwal in 2013, offering budget accommodation and home-stays.

 

• J&K's tourism department has separately promoted schemes such as 'Mission Youth' and various rural/border tourism circuits to boost local livelihoods in remote areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Weaving a Better Future (Option 1): Not the name associated with the OYO-J&K rural tourism partnership.

 

• Shared Planet (Option 3): Not related to this initiative.

 

• United India (Option 4): Not related to this initiative.

question: Chief Minister Shramik Kalyan Prakalp scheme was launched by Amit Shah for women of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched the 'Mukhyamantri Chaa Sramik Kalyan Prakalp' (Chief Minister Tea Workers' Welfare Scheme) for the welfare of women tea garden workers of Tripura. (मुख्यमंत्री चा श्रमिक कल्याण प्रकल्प — त्रिपुरा)

 

• The scheme is aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of tea garden labourers, particularly women workers, in Tripura's tea industry.

 

• The launch took place as part of the Union Government's outreach in Tripura, a state with a significant tea-garden workforce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tripura is one of India's notable tea-producing states, along with Assam and West Bengal, though on a smaller scale.

 

• Amit Shah has, on separate occasions, also inaugurated infrastructure projects in Tripura such as the National Forensic Sciences University campus in Agartala.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Not the state associated with this scheme.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): Not the state associated with this scheme.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Not the state associated with this scheme.

question: Players that stop dribbling in handball have to pass or shot within:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In handball, once a player stops dribbling and holds the ball, they must pass or shoot within 3 seconds (and within three steps), failing which it is ruled a foul. (हैंडबॉल — 3 सेकंड नियम)

 

• Handball is a 7-a-side team sport (6 outfield players + 1 goalkeeper) played on a court measuring 40m x 20m, with the goal being to throw a ball into the opponent's goal.

 

• Other key handball rules include the 3-step rule (a player may take a maximum of three steps while holding the ball without dribbling) and the goal area (6-metre line), which only the goalkeeper may enter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Handball is governed internationally by the International Handball Federation (IHF), headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

 

• Handball has been an Olympic sport since the 1972 Munich Olympics (men's), with women's handball added at the 1976 Montreal Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 second (Option 1): Not the applicable time limit for this rule.

 

• 30 second (Option 2): Not the applicable time limit for this rule.

 

• 10 second (Option 3): Not the applicable time limit for this rule.

question: Which of the following sequence is correct with respect to the Delhi Dynasties?
option_1: Khalji dynasty, Lodi dynasty, Sayyid dynasty
option_2: Tughluq dynasty, Khalji dynasty, Sayyid dynasty
option_3: Early Turkish Rulers, Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty
option_4: Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty, Tughluq dynasty
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty, Tughluq dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Delhi was ruled successively by Rajput dynasties (such as the Tomaras and Chauhans) before the Turkish conquest, followed by the Delhi Sultanate, whose dynasties in chronological order were Mamluk/Slave (1206-1290) → Khalji (1290-1320) → Tughluq (1320-1414) → Sayyid (1414-1451) → Lodi (1451-1526). (दिल्ली सल्तनत — खिलजी के बाद तुगलक वंश)

 

• Thus, the correct broad chronological sequence among the given options is Rajput dynasties → Khalji dynasty → Tughluq dynasty.

 

• The Khalji dynasty was founded by Jalaluddin Khalji in 1290 and its most notable ruler was Alauddin Khalji; the Tughluq dynasty was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq in 1320.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Slave (Mamluk) dynasty, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206, was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, preceding the Khalji dynasty.

 

• The Delhi Sultanate ended in 1526 when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, establishing the Mughal Empire.

 

NOTE

 

• Khalji dynasty, Lodi dynasty, Sayyid dynasty (Option 1): Incorrect order — the Sayyid dynasty preceded the Lodi dynasty, not the other way around.

 

• Tughluq dynasty, Khalji dynasty, Sayyid dynasty (Option 2): Incorrect order — the Khalji dynasty preceded the Tughluq dynasty.

 

• Early Turkish Rulers, Rajput dynasties, Khalji dynasty (Option 3): Incorrect order — the Rajput dynasties ruled before the Turkish conquest, not after it.

question: Which of the following is NOT a classification of E-Commerce?
solution_text:
The correct answer is D2D (Distributor-to-Distributor).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D2D (Distributor-to-Distributor) is not a recognised/standard classification of E-Commerce business models. (ई-कॉमर्स वर्गीकरण — D2D मान्य श्रेणी नहीं)

 

• The standard classifications of E-Commerce, based on the parties involved in a transaction, are B2B (Business-to-Business), B2C (Business-to-Consumer), C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer), and C2B (Consumer-to-Business).

 

• Other recognised extended categories include B2G (Business-to-Government) and G2C (Government-to-Citizen).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples: B2B – Alibaba; B2C – Amazon, Flipkart; C2C – OLX, eBay (peer-to-peer resale platforms).

 

• India's e-commerce sector is regulated under policies of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), part of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

 

NOTE

 

• B2C (Option 1): A valid, well-recognised E-Commerce classification (Business-to-Consumer).

 

• C2C (Option 3): A valid, well-recognised E-Commerce classification (Consumer-to-Consumer).

 

• B2B (Option 4): A valid, well-recognised E-Commerce classification (Business-to-Business).

question: _______ takes oath as new Meghalaya Governor in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B.D. Mishra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brigadier (Retd.) B.D. Mishra, who was already serving as the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, took additional charge and was sworn in as the Governor of Meghalaya on 4 October 2022. (बी.डी. मिश्रा — मेघालय के राज्यपाल)

 

• He succeeded Satya Pal Malik, who had earlier held additional charge of Meghalaya before Mishra's appointment.

 

• The oath was administered by the Chief Justice of the Meghalaya High Court at Raj Bhavan, Shillong.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• B.D. Mishra is a retired Indian Army Brigadier who has held gubernatorial charge of both Arunachal Pradesh and (additionally) Meghalaya.

 

• The Governor of a state in India is appointed by the President and serves as the constitutional/nominal head of the state executive under Articles 153-162 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• A K Anil Kumar (Option 2): Not the Governor of Meghalaya in October 2022.

 

• Prashant Kumar (Option 3): Not the Governor of Meghalaya in October 2022.

 

• Sunil Barthwal (Option 4): Not the Governor of Meghalaya in October 2022; he is an IAS officer who has held various bureaucratic posts.

question: There are ______ main types of cell division.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• There are two main types of cell division: Mitosis and Meiosis. (कोशिका विभाजन — समसूत्री और अर्धसूत्री)

 

• Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells from a single parent cell and is responsible for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.

 

• Meiosis produces four genetically distinct haploid daughter cells (gametes) from a single diploid parent cell, and is essential for sexual reproduction, involving two successive divisions (Meiosis I and Meiosis II).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before either type of division, the cell undergoes Interphase (G1, S, and G2 phases), during which DNA is replicated.

 

• Amitosis (direct cell division, seen in some prokaryotes/simple organisms) is sometimes mentioned separately but is not counted among the two principal types of cell division in eukaryotes.

 

NOTE

 

• 4, 3, 5 (Options 1, 3, 4): Incorrect counts — biology recognises only two main types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis.

question: The first session of Indian National congress was held at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first session of the Indian National Congress (INC) was held in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — प्रथम अधिवेशन, बॉम्बे)

 

• It was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and attended by 72 delegates.

 

• The INC was founded by Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, with the initial support of leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji and Dinshaw Edulji Wacha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The INC was originally scheduled to meet in Pune but was shifted to Bombay due to a cholera outbreak in Pune.

 

• The famous Surat Split of 1907 divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists, but that was the site of a later, not the first, session.

 

NOTE

 

• Madras (Option 2): Hosted later INC sessions (e.g., 1887, 1898), not the first.

 

• Calcutta (Option 3): Hosted several later sessions (e.g., 1886, 1917, 1928), not the first.

 

• Surat (Option 4): Site of the historic 1907 INC session where the party split, not the first session.

question: An electric current is expressed by a unit called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ampere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric current is measured in ampere (A), the SI base unit named after French physicist André-Marie Ampère. (एम्पियर — विद्युत धारा की इकाई)

 

• One ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second through a conductor.

 

• Electric current is measured using an instrument called an ammeter, connected in series in a circuit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ampere is one of the seven SI base units, along with the metre, kilogram, second, kelvin, mole, and candela.

 

• Related electrical quantities: Voltage is measured in volts, Resistance in ohms, and Power in watts.

 

NOTE

 

• meter (Option 1): The SI unit of length/distance, not electric current.

 

• watt (Option 3): The SI unit of power (rate of energy transfer), not current.

 

• joule (Option 4): The SI unit of energy/work, not current.

question: How thick is the lithosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 to 200 kilometres.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The lithosphere — the rigid, outermost shell of the Earth comprising the crust and the uppermost solid part of the mantle — is approximately 10 to 200 kilometres thick, varying between oceanic and continental regions. (स्थलमंडल — पृथ्वी की सबसे बाहरी ठोस परत)

 

• Oceanic lithosphere is typically thinner (about 50-100 km), while continental lithosphere can be much thicker, extending up to about 150-200 km beneath stable continental interiors (cratons).

 

• The lithosphere is broken into several rigid tectonic plates that float and move over the underlying, more plastic asthenosphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Below the lithosphere lies the asthenosphere, a partially molten, ductile layer of the upper mantle over which the lithospheric plates move (the basis of plate tectonics).

 

• Earth's interior, from surface to centre, is broadly divided into the crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core.

 

NOTE

 

• 25 to 45 kilometres, 10 to 25 kilometres, 5 to 10 kilometres (Options 1, 2, 4): These ranges understate the actual thickness of the lithosphere, which extends well beyond the crust alone into the uppermost rigid mantle.

question: Who among the following is related to the musical instrument Santoor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a legendary Indian classical musician credited with popularising the santoor — a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer traditionally from Jammu and Kashmir — as a solo Hindustani classical instrument. (संतूर — पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा)

 

• He famously collaborated with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia as the duo 'Shiv-Hari', who also composed music for several Bollywood films.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and passed away in May 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The santoor was traditionally used to accompany Sufiana Mausiqi (Sufi music) in Kashmir before Pandit Shivkumar Sharma adapted it for Hindustani classical solo performance.

 

• Other instrument-artist associations: Sitar – Pandit Ravi Shankar; Sarod – Ustad Amjad Ali Khan; Tabla – Ustad Zakir Hussain.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Ravishankar Prasad (Option 2): Not primarily associated with the santoor; distinct from the famous sitarist Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (Option 3): A renowned flute (bansuri) maestro, not the santoor.

 

• Pandit Jasraj (Option 4): A celebrated Hindustani vocalist of the Mewati Gharana, not an instrumentalist associated with the santoor.

question: Chemical formula of magnesium oxide is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is MgO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Magnesium oxide, commonly known as magnesia, has the chemical formula MgO. (मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड — MgO)

 

• It is formed when magnesium metal burns in oxygen/air, producing a bright white light — a classic reaction: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

 

• MgO is a white, odourless solid used as a refractory material, in antacid and laxative medicines, and as a dietary magnesium supplement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• When magnesium oxide reacts with water, it forms magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂, commonly known as milk of magnesia, used as an antacid.

 

• Magnesium has the atomic number 12 and belongs to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) of the periodic table.

 

NOTE

 

• MgCO3 (Option 1): This is magnesium carbonate, a different compound, not magnesium oxide.

 

• MgO2 (Option 2): This would represent magnesium peroxide, not the common oxide of magnesium.

 

• Mg(OH)2 (Option 4): This is magnesium hydroxide, formed when MgO reacts with water, not magnesium oxide itself.

question: The Constitution forbids employment of children below the age of ______ years in dangerous jobs like factories and mines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous occupation. (अनुच्छेद 24 — 14 वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों का नियोजन निषेध)

 

• Article 24 is part of the Fundamental Rights, specifically under the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24).

 

• This constitutional provision is reinforced by laws such as the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended in 2016), alongside Article 21A / Article 45, which provide for free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 completely bans employment of children below 14 years in any occupation, and regulates the employment of adolescents (14-18 years) in hazardous occupations.

 

• Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar).

 

NOTE

 

• 15, 16, 18 (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not match the constitutionally specified minimum age of 14 years under Article 24, though 18 is the age up to which employment in hazardous occupations is regulated for adolescents.

question: Which of the following is not a natural fibre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rayon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rayon is a man-made (regenerated/semi-synthetic) fibre, manufactured from cellulose (typically wood pulp) through a chemical process, and is not classified as a natural fibre. (रेयॉन — कृत्रिम रेशा)

 

• Rayon is often called 'artificial silk' because of its silk-like sheen, and was one of the first man-made fibres to be developed.

 

• Linen, Cotton, and Jute, by contrast, are all natural plant fibres: linen from the flax plant, cotton from the cotton plant's seed bolls, and jute from the jute plant's stem (bast fibre).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural fibres are broadly classified as plant fibres (cotton, jute, linen/flax, hemp) and animal fibres (wool, silk).

 

• Other man-made fibres include nylon, polyester, and acrylic, which are fully synthetic (petroleum-based), unlike rayon which is semi-synthetic (cellulose-based).

 

NOTE

 

• Linen (Option 1): A natural fibre obtained from the flax plant.

 

• Cotton (Option 2): A natural fibre obtained from the cotton plant.

 

• Jute (Option 4): A natural fibre obtained from the jute plant, widely grown in West Bengal, known as the 'Golden Fibre'.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the election of the President of India?
option_1: He/She is indirectly elected by the elected MLAs and MPs.
option_2: The President is elected for a period of five years.
option_3: All doubts and disputes in connection with the President's election can be inquired into and decided by both the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
option_4: The election takes place in accordance with the principle of proportional representation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All doubts and disputes in connection with the President's election can be inquired into and decided by both the Supreme Court and the High Courts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 71 of the Constitution, all doubts and disputes relating to the election of the President (and Vice-President) are inquired into and decided only by the Supreme Court of India, whose decision is final — High Courts have no jurisdiction in this matter. (राष्ट्रपति चुनाव विवाद — केवल सर्वोच्च न्यायालय)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament (MPs) and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) of States and Union Territories (Delhi and Puducherry).

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the President's term of office is five years (Article 56), though they can be re-elected.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: the election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with voting by secret ballot (Article 55).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3, as it wrongly includes the High Courts, which have no role in adjudicating presidential election disputes.

 

Additional Information

 

• The value of votes of MLAs and MPs in the Electoral College is calculated based on the population of the state and the number of elected members, ensuring uniformity of representation across states.

 

• Nominated members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies, and members of Legislative Councils, do not participate in the President's election.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Correctly describes the indirect election of the President and is therefore not the answer to this 'NOT correct' question.

 

• Option 2: Correctly states the five-year term and is therefore not the answer.

 

• Option 4: Correctly describes the proportional representation/single transferable vote system and is therefore not the answer.

question: Which of the following is celebrated as the New Year in Tamil Nadu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puthandu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Puthandu, also known as the Tamil New Year, is celebrated in Tamil Nadu, marking the first day of the Tamil month of Chithirai (mid-April). (புத்தாண்டு — तमिल नववर्ष)

 

• It is celebrated with rituals like Kanni (viewing an auspicious arrangement of items first thing in the morning), preparing traditional dishes like Manga Pachadi, and visiting temples.

 

• Puthandu usually falls on 14 April, coinciding with similar New Year festivals celebrated across South and Southeast Asia based on the solar calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pongal is a separate, major harvest festival of Tamil Nadu celebrated in mid-January, dedicated to the Sun God (Surya).

 

• Similar New Year festivals celebrated around mid-April in other regions include Vishu (Kerala), Bihu (Assam), and Baisakhi (Punjab).

 

NOTE

 

• Pongal (Option 1): A major Tamil harvest festival in January, not the Tamil New Year.

 

• Ugadi (Option 3): The New Year festival of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka, not Tamil Nadu.

 

• Onam (Option 4): A major harvest festival of Kerala, not the Tamil New Year.

question: In the early eleventh century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple and filled it with a Sun-pedestal seized from the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chalukyas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the early 11th century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple at his new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and filled it with prized war trophies, including a 'Sun-pedestal' seized from the Chalukyas, whom he had defeated. (राजेंद्र प्रथम — चालुक्यों से जीता सूर्य-पीठ)

 

• This episode illustrates how Chola temples were often repositories of prized war booty, reflecting the political rivalry between the Cholas and the Western Chalukyas.

 

• Rajendra I (son of Rajaraja I) was a great Chola conqueror who led naval expeditions as far as Southeast Asia (Sri Vijaya) and extended Chola power up to the Ganga, earning the title 'Gangaikonda Chola'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram built by Rajendra I is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, part of the 'Great Living Chola Temples' along with the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur (built by Rajaraja I) and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.

 

• The Cholas were prolific temple builders, and their temples often served as centres of economic and administrative activity besides religious worship.

 

NOTE

 

• Palas (Option 1): A dynasty that ruled over Bengal and Bihar; not the source of the Sun-pedestal trophy.

 

• Vakatakas (Option 2): A Deccan dynasty of the 3rd-6th century CE, too early to be relevant to Rajendra I's 11th-century conquest.

 

• Kalingas (Option 4): Refers to the region/dynasty of ancient Odisha, not the source of this particular war trophy.

question: Which of the following offices was NOT held by the poet Harishena?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagara-shreshthi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harishena, the court poet of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta and composer of the Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), held several important offices, but 'Nagara-shreshthi' (chief of the city/merchant guild) was not one of them. (हरिषेण — समुद्रगुप्त के दरबारी कवि)

 

• According to the Prayaga Prashasti, Harishena held the offices of Kumar-amatya (a high-ranking minister), Sandhi-vigrahika (minister of peace and war/foreign affairs), and Maha-danda-nayaka (chief justice/commander of the army/police).

 

• The Prayaga Prashasti, composed by Harishena and inscribed on the Allahabad Pillar, is one of the most important sources for the reign and conquests of Samudragupta, often called the 'Napoleon of India'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'shreshthi' generally referred to the head of a merchant guild in ancient India, an office distinct from the court/administrative titles held by Harishena.

 

• The Gupta period (4th-6th century CE) is often called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India, marked by advances in art, science, and literature.

 

NOTE

 

• Sandhi-vigrahika (Option 1): An office actually held by Harishena, dealing with foreign affairs (peace and war).

 

• Maha-danda-nayaka (Option 2): An office actually held by Harishena, related to justice/military command.

 

• Kumar-amatya (Option 4): An office actually held by Harishena, a high-ranking ministerial post.

question: ______ is found in association with rocks composed of calcium carbonates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Limestone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Limestone is a sedimentary rock predominantly composed of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), and is found in association with rocks and mineral deposits formed from calcium and magnesium carbonate. (चूना पत्थर — कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट युक्त चट्टान)

 

• It is formed mainly from the skeletal remains of marine organisms such as coral and foraminifera, or through the chemical precipitation of calcium carbonate from water.

 

• Limestone is a vital raw material for the cement industry, and is also used in iron smelting (as a flux), in the manufacture of lime, and in construction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common varieties/related rocks of calcium carbonate composition include chalk, marble (metamorphosed limestone), and dolomite (calcium-magnesium carbonate).

 

• Major limestone deposits in India are found in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka.

 

NOTE

 

• Gold (Option 2): A native metallic element typically found in quartz veins and alluvial deposits, not specifically associated with calcium carbonate rocks.

 

• Iron (Option 3): Found mainly in oxide ores like hematite and magnetite in banded iron formations, not specifically in calcium carbonate rocks.

 

• Diamond (Option 4): Found in kimberlite and lamproite pipes (igneous rocks), not associated with calcium carbonate rocks.
